The informal estimate during the incident was "maybe around 20 customers" affected, based on a quick database check by Chloe Dupont and supported as a ballpark by Raj Patel [NL-022#NL-022-S03]. The final impact, established later by the official postmortem after a complete audit of database transaction logs, was exactly 17 customer workspaces directly affected by the upload pipeline and indexing queue outage [NL-022#NL-022-S03]. The postmortem also emphasized that the postmortem database audit is the sole authority for customer-impact metrics and that internal engineering guesses should not be published before audits are complete [NL-013#NL-013-S09].

Corrective work addressing recurrence includes:

- Enforcing a maximum of 5 retries for document processing jobs with exponential backoff and randomized jitter, completed March 15, 2026 [NL-013#NL-013-S07].
- Mandating multi-stage, lock-free schema migrations for tables larger than 100,000 rows, with `NOT VALID` foreign keys verified separately, completed March 16, 2026 [NL-013#NL-013-S07].
- Implementing granular Redis queue monitoring alerts for retry frequencies and worker connection states [NL-013#NL-013-S07][NL-013#NL-013-S08].
- Conducting ingestion load testing under connection-starvation scenarios [NL-013#NL-013-S07][NL-013#NL-013-S08].
- Separating database connection pools for write-heavy background tasks and read-heavy user queries [NL-013#NL-013-S07][NL-013#NL-013-S08].
- Revising the SRE runbook with Redis queue backups, manual connection purging, read-only failovers, quarterly disaster recovery drills, and alerting on-call engineers within 120 seconds of latency spikes [NL-013#NL-013-S09].
- Shifting engineering mindset to "fail gracefully with backoff" and maintaining rapid, one-click rollback capabilities [NL-013#NL-013-S09].
